claims.text:
Ioreth means "old woman" in Sindarin; iaur ("old") plus feminine ending -eth. In draft, Tolkien had spelt her name Yoreth.
Like "Gamling", it was specifically chosen to suit the character of the old nurse.
thumb|left|150px|Ioreth in [[The Lord of the Rings Online]]
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Letter to a Mr. Joukes dated August 28, 1967", published in Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull, The Lord of the Rings: A Reader's Companion, p. 579

claims.text: Ioreth was originally from Imloth Melui in Lossarnach, but moved to Minas Tirith and worked in the Houses of Healing. By she was the oldest woman working there and was well versed in old lore. Upon seeing the illness-stricken Faramir, she said that she wished there was still a king in Gondor, remarking "For it is said in old lore: The hands of the king are the hands of a healer." Gandalf heard this, and brought Aragorn to the Houses of Healing, where he was able to heal many of the sick. Ioreth was very talkative, which annoyed Aragorn and Gandalf.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "The Houses of Healing"
